questions.question_text: Design an algorithm that reads a student's total score and displays "Pass" if the score is 50 or more, otherwise "Fail". Write the algorithm using pseudocode and draw the corresponding flowchart.
questions.model_answer:
Start
Use variable: score
Input score
IF score >= 50
    print("Pass")
ELSE
    print("Fail")
Stop
Flowchart: Terminal Start; Input/Output symbol for input score; Decision symbol for score >= 50; two branches: true leads to Input/Output print("Pass"), false leads to Input/Output print("Fail"); both branches lead to Terminal Stop.

questions.question_text: Explain the difference between an interpreter and a compiler as presented in the lecture, and list the three steps that Java programs normally go through.
questions.model_answer: An interpreter reads one statement from the source code, translates it to machine code, and executes it right away. A compiler translates the entire source code into a machine-code file, which is then executed. Java programs normally go through three steps: 1) Source Codes (.java) – write source code using an editor or IDE; 2) Java Bytecodes (.class) – use Java compiler to compile/build; 3) Run/Execute – use Java Runtime to run the bytecode.

grading_rubric.description: States that interpreter translates and executes one statement at a time.
States that compiler translates entire source code into machine-code file before execution.
Lists Source Codes (.java), Java Bytecodes (.class), and Run/Execute.

questions.grading_notes: Accept equivalent wording that reflects the lecture's definitions and steps.

questions.question_text: Explain the rules for naming a Java class. Provide two valid and two invalid class name examples and state why each is valid or invalid.
questions.model_answer: A class name is a sequence of characters that consists of letters, digits, underscores (_), and dollar signs ($). A class name cannot: start with a digit, be a reserved word, or contain spaces. Valid examples: Student (letters only), Student_Class (letters and underscore). Invalid examples: 123student (starts with a digit), Student Class (contains a space). Other valid examples include Student1, $StudentClass, _StudentClass1. Other invalid examples include class, public, void (reserved words), 1StudentClass (starts with digit).

grading_rubric.description: States letters, digits, underscores, and dollar signs are allowed.
Lists cannot start with digit, cannot be reserved word, cannot contain spaces.
Provides two valid class names and explains why they are valid.
Provides two invalid class names and explains why they are invalid.

questions.grading_notes: Accept any valid and invalid examples that follow the lecture's rules.

questions.question_text: Describe the special symbols in Java and their meanings as presented in the lecture: {}, (), [], //, "", ;.
questions.model_answer: The special symbols are: {} opening and closing braces – denote a block to enclose statements; () opening and closing parentheses – used with methods; [] opening and closing brackets – denotes an array; // double slashes – precedes a comment line; "" opening and closing quotation marks – enclosing a string; ; semicolon – marks the end of a statement.

States they precede a comment line.
States they enclose a string.

Covers all six symbols accurately.
